page_title: Borne — MAME arcade and PC classics on the Mac

sources.entry: Borne - Native front end for MAME and classic PC games (Doom, Quake, Duke Nukem 3D), in the spirit of MAMEUI, with the emulator and engines included. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/gpasa/borne)

summary.name: Borne
summary.one_liner: Borne is a free, GPL-3.0 licensed native Mac front end that organizes MAME arcade games and classic PC games (Doom, Quake, Duke Nukem 3D) and launches them with a double-click.
use_cases: Organize and browse a large MAME arcade ROM collection on a Mac
Launch Doom, Quake and similar PC classics without using a terminal
Play Doom for free using Freedoom
Keep a game library on an external drive while installing favorites locally
Filter arcade games by manufacturer, year or vertical screen
summary.what_it_does: Borne scans a user-supplied arcade ROM folder and PC games folder, then presents them in a browsable, searchable interface. It bundles MAME 0.289 with more than 43,000 machines and can filter by availability, favorites, manufacturer, year, and vertical screen. For PC games, it finds game files, groups add-ons with their parent game, and launches modern engines such as those for Doom, Quake, and Duke Nukem 3D. Games launch with a double-click, showing a key reminder, and Esc returns to Borne. Borne reads game folders without writing to them, storing settings, saves, and screenshots in the user folder.
notable: Bundles MAME 0.289 and game engines so no separate emulator install is needed
Read-only access to game folders; saves and settings kept in user folder
Freedoom, a free Doom-compatible game, can be downloaded in one click
Open source under GPL-3.0 with code on GitHub
caveats: Does not include any games; users must supply their own ROMs and PC game files
Independent project, not part of the MAME project
